# Pinned to jj-lib's version in vcs/Cargo.toml — bump both together. Exported into every job's
# `run:` steps automatically (GitHub Actions workflow-level env), so `cli`, `vcs-core`, and `app`
# all install the same jj from one declared value instead of independently-typed literals.
env:
  JJ_VERSION: 0.43.0

jobs:
  cli:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      # `jj` is what TestAddProjectCreate_ExistingJJRepoUsedAsIs / TestDeleteProjectSafetyJJ_* shell
      # out to — both `t.Skip` silently without it, so without this step they never ran in CI at
      # all. Same pattern as the `vcs-core` job below (apt has no jj package, hence the release
      # tarball). $JJ_VERSION comes from the workflow-level env: above.
      - name: Install jj
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \
            | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ./jj
          jj --version

      # golangci-lint subsumes `go vet` (govet) and the gofmt check (gofmt linter). Installed
      # with `go install` so it's built with the project's Go toolchain (go.mod), matching local.
      - name: Lint
        run: |
          go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/cmd/golangci-lint@v1.64.8
          "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/golangci-lint" run

      - name: Build
        run: go build -o workroom .

      - name: Test
        run: go test ./...

jobs:
  cli:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Matrix over jj CLI versions the Go tests shell out to (see the "Install jj" step below) —
    # NOT the same axis as $JJ_VERSION above, which stays the single version `app`'s fixed-cost
    # macOS job installs. This caught a real bug (2026-08-16): fixtures shelling to `jj` assumed
    # 0.44's "auto-advance @ off an immutable tip after push" and silently broke on 0.43, where
    # `jj` behaves differently. Keep this list and vcs-core's in sync — both exercise the same
    # CLI-shelling concern from different languages. Bump when jj cuts a new release worth
    # covering; no need to chase every patch release.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        jj-version: ["0.43.0", "0.44.0"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      # `jj` is what TestAddProjectCreate_ExistingJJRepoUsedAsIs / TestDeleteProjectSafetyJJ_* shell
      # out to — both `t.Skip` silently without it, so without this step they never ran in CI at
      # all. Same pattern as the `vcs-core` job below (apt has no jj package, hence the release
      # tarball).
      - name: Install jj
        env:
          JJ_VERSION: ${{ matrix.jj-version }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \
            | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ./jj
          jj --version

run: go build -o workroom .

      - name: Test
        run: go test ./...

  # The Rust VCS core's own tests (jj-lib reads against real throwaway jj repos, incl. the
  # working-copy snapshot + conflict classification). Its own Linux job rather than a step in `app`:
  # off the macOS critical path (it was ~3min of it on a cold run), Linux minutes are 10x cheaper,
  # and it's the only thing testing the core away from Apple targets.
  vcs-core:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # protoc is a build-time dep of jj-lib. The `jj` CLI is what the working_status fixtures shell
      # out to for repo setup (and the test SKIPS silently without it, so it must be installed) —
      # apt has no jj package, hence the release tarball. $JJ_VERSION comes from the
      # workflow-level env: above.
      - name: Install protoc + jj
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq protobuf-compiler
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/releases/download/v$JJ_VERSION/jj-v$JJ_VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \
            | sudo tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ./jj
          jj --version

      # Pinned for the lint gates below, unlike the `app` job (which deliberately tracks the runner's
      # rustc so a toolchain bump invalidates its output cache). rustfmt's layout and clippy's lint set
      # both change between releases, so an unpinned toolchain makes `--check` and `-D warnings` fail
      # when GitHub rolls its image rather than when someone's code is wrong. Same reasoning as the
      # pinned golangci-lint in `cli`. Keep in step with the local toolchain.
      - name: Install Rust 1.96.1
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install 1.96.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
          rustup default 1.96.1

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: vcs

      # Ordered cheapest-first so a formatting nit doesn't wait on the jj-lib crate graph.
      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --manifest-path vcs/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

fix(vcs-tests): make jj remote fixtures version-agnostic, matrix jj CLI in CI

master's CI went red on jj 0.43.0 (the pinned version): two
VCSRemoteIntegrationTests fixtures relied on `jj describe` in place,
assuming jj 0.44's "auto-advance @ off an immutable tip after push" —

already-pushed, immutable commit instead of creating new work. Replaced
with `jj new main`, which produces the same fresh, unbookmarked commit
either way — verified against both 0.43.0 and 0.44.0 by hand (Homebrew
symlink swap) and via the full test suite.

Added a jj-version matrix (0.43.0/0.44.0) to the cheap Linux `cli` and
`vcs-core` jobs so this class of drift is caught automatically; `app`
(10x the runner cost) keeps installing the single lockstep-with-jj-lib
version.

content.text: Found it — my own bug. `makePipe()` only set the *write* end non-blocking; the read loop calls `SessionIO.read(readFD)` on a still-blocking read descriptor, so once buffered bytes are drained it blocks forever in a real `read()` syscall. That's the hang — not a toolchain wedge. Killing the stuck processes and fixing it.

+    // Both ends non-blocking: the write end so `drain` sees a real `wouldBlock` instead of

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Shared, app-wide project data: the project list plus everything derived from it that is
4	/// identical across windows — root branch/bookmark labels, the VCS/CI status cache, GitHub-CLI
5	/// availability, and the in-flight project busy set. Extracted from `AppStore` (issue #70) so that
6	/// multiple per-window `AppStore`s can share one project list while each keeps its own selection,
7	/// terminals, splits, history, and run state.
8	///
9	/// This first step is **storage-only and behaviour-preserving**: `AppStore` proxies these
10	/// properties straight through to here and re-publishes the store's `objectWillChange`, so the
11	/// single shared `AppStore` still behaves exactly as before. The CLI/load logic stays on `AppStore`
12	/// for now (it mutates these via the proxies); per-window construction and the multi-window wiring
13	/// land in a follow-up.
14	@MainActor
15	final class ProjectStore: ObservableObject {
16	  /// The shared instance used in production (every window's `AppStore` points at it). Tests
17	  /// construct an isolated `AppStore()`, which gets its own fresh `ProjectStore`, so they never
18	  /// pollute this singleton or each other.
19	  static let shared = ProjectStore()
20	
21	  /// The list of configured projects (from the CLI's `~/.config/workroom/config.json`). The one
22	  /// piece of state shared across all windows.
23	  @Published var projects: [Project] = []
24	
25	  /// Per-project resolved root branch/bookmark labels, hydrated asynchronously after each load.
26	  @Published var rootRefs: [Project.ID: RootRef] = [:]
27	
28	  /// Per-workroom (and per-root) VCS + CI status driving the ambient badges and the Changes panel
29	  /// (issue #24), keyed by `SidebarID`. Resolved app-side, best-effort/"last checked". Shared so two
30	  /// windows showing the same workroom report a consistent badge and don't double the probes.
31	  @Published var workroomStatuses: [SidebarID: WorkroomStatus] = [:]
32	
33	  /// Whether the GitHub CLI is usable for the PR/CI probes (machine-global). Optimistic default so
34	  /// no warning flashes before the first check.
35	  @Published var githubCLIStatus: GitHubCLIStatus = .available
36	
37	  /// Owns the `gh auth status` probe: its freshness clock AND its single-flight, so N windows share
38	  /// one `gh` and the staleness check can't interleave with the write the way a bare timestamp on
39	  /// this class did. `githubCLIStatus` above is the SwiftUI-observable mirror of what it decided.
40	  ///
41	  /// A `var` purely so tests can swap in an instance with millisecond TTLs; production never
42	  /// reassigns it.
43	  var ghAuthCache = GitHubAuthCache()
44	
45	  /// Owns the git/jj `--version` probe: its freshness clock AND its single-flight, per tool, so N
46	  /// windows share one probe each rather than racing two. `vcsToolReport` on `AppStore` mirrors what
47	  /// this decided (per-window, since `apply(projects)` runs per-window even though the underlying
48	  /// facts are machine-wide).
49	  ///
50	  /// A `var` for the same reason `ghAuthCache` is: tests swap in an instance with millisecond TTLs;
51	  /// production never reassigns it.
52	  var vcsToolVersionCache = VCSToolVersionCache()
53	
54	  /// Project paths with an in-flight create/delete (for per-row progress + disabling).
55	  @Published var busyProjects: Set<String> = []
56	
57	  /// Target ids of workrooms whose create is still in flight — from the "created" event until the
58	  /// create flow ends (issue #116). A workroom here must not be deleted: its setup script is running
59	  /// against the worktree. Shared across windows so a delete from ANY window is blocked, not just the
60	  /// creating one.
61	  @Published var creatingWorkrooms: Set<TerminalTarget.ID> = []
62	
63	  /// Sidebar rows with a commit in flight, for the per-row button state.
64	  ///
65	  /// Shared across windows for the reason `creatingWorkrooms` is: `AppStore` is per WINDOW, but
66	  /// `JJSnapshotGate` and the `index.lock` contention it exists to prevent are per PROCESS. Held on
67	  /// the window's own store, a second window's 15s sweep, FSEvents lane and Refresh button all saw an
68	  /// empty set and kept probing a repo mid-write.
69	  @Published var committingTargets: Set<SidebarID> = []
70	
71	  /// How many commits are in flight against each project root, which is what the read lanes actually
72	  /// have to stand clear of.
73	  ///
74	  /// Keyed by project root, not by row: the gate serializes on the project root, and a git worktree's
75	  /// index and refs live in the MAIN repo — so a commit in workroom A contends with a status probe of
76	  /// workroom B of the same project, which a per-row check waved straight through. Counted rather than
77	  /// a `Set` because the app's premise is N parallel workrooms, so two of one project can legitimately
78	  /// commit at once and the first to finish must not clear the other's suppression.
79	  @Published var committingProjectRoots: [String: Int] = [:]
80	
81	  /// How many writes (commit, fetch, push, or pull) are in flight against each project root,
82	  /// across every window. Checked by the write ACTIONS THEMSELVES before starting — not just
83	  /// by read lanes — so a second write on the same project root is refused outright rather than
84	  /// queuing into `JJSnapshotGate` and possibly racing a live one past its wedge-detection
85	  /// ceiling (VCS-foundation eng-review: the gate's `maxChainWait` self-heal is far shorter than
86	  /// fetch/pull's own timeouts, so two windows could otherwise both queue a write and run them
87	  /// concurrently on the shared `.git`). Distinct from `committingProjectRoots`, which exists for
88	  /// a different reason (suppressing READ lanes during a commit specifically) and keeps its own
89	  /// narrower role unchanged; this counter is the umbrella that all four write kinds share.
90	  @Published var writingProjectRoots: [String: Int] = [:]

3	/// Errors surfaced from running the bundled `workroom` binary.
4	enum WorkroomCLIError: LocalizedError {
5	  case binaryMissing
6	  case timedOut
7	  case decodeFailed(raw: String)
8	  /// A structured error from the CLI's --json contract.
9	  case cli(kind: String, message: String)
10	  /// Non-zero exit without a decodable JSON error envelope.
11	  case nonzero(code: Int32, stderr: String)
12	
13	  var errorDescription: String? {
14	    switch self {
15	    case .binaryMissing:
16	      return "The bundled 'workroom' helper was not found in the app bundle."
17	    case .timedOut:
18	      return "The workroom command timed out."
19	    case .decodeFailed(let raw):
20	      return "Could not parse the workroom response: \(raw.prefix(200))"
21	    case .cli(_, let message):
22	      return message

25	    }

29	  var kind: String? {

35	private struct CLIResult {
36	  let stdout: Data
37	  let stderr: String
38	  let exitCode: Int32
39	  /// The timeout fired and we `terminate()`d the child.
40	  let timedOut: Bool
41	  /// The child was killed by a signal (`terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`) rather than
42	  /// exiting normally — e.g. our own timeout's SIGTERM, or a SIGTERM the system delivers around
43	  /// sleep/wake. `exitCode` is then the *signal number* (SIGTERM = 15), NOT a CLI exit status.

47	/// Lock-guarded state shared across the drain/timeout/termination callbacks. A
48	/// reference type so the @Sendable closures capture an immutable `let` and mutate
49	/// through it, rather than capturing mutable vars (a data race under Swift 6).
50	private final class RunState: @unchecked Sendable {
51	  private let lock = NSLock()
52	  private var _stdout = Data()
53	  private var _finished = false
54	  private var _timedOut = false
55	
56	  func setStdout(_ d: Data) {
57	    lock.lock()
58	    _stdout = d
59	    lock.unlock()
60	  }
61	  func markFinished() {
62	    lock.lock()
63	    _finished = true
64	    lock.unlock()
65	  }
66	  func markTimedOut() {
67	    lock.lock()
68	    _timedOut = true
69	    lock.unlock()
70	  }
71	  var isFinished: Bool {
72	    lock.lock()
73	    defer { lock.unlock() }
74	    return _finished
75	  }
76	  var timedOut: Bool {
77	    lock.lock()
78	    defer { lock.unlock() }
79	    return _timedOut
80	  }
81	  var stdout: Data {
82	    lock.lock()
83	    defer { lock.unlock() }
84	    return _stdout
85	  }
86	}

88	/// Reads stderr incrementally, splitting on newlines so NDJSON log events surface
89	/// live (rather than only after the process exits). It also keeps the raw bytes for
90	/// the fallback error path (a non-zero exit without a decodable stdout envelope).
91	/// `@unchecked Sendable` because the file handle's readability callbacks are
92	/// serialized, and the lock guards the buffers regardless.
93	private final class StderrCollector: @unchecked Sendable {
94	  private let lock = NSLock()
95	  private var raw = Data()
96	  private var pending = Data()
97	  private let onEvent: ((StreamEvent) -> Void)?
98	
99	  init(onEvent: ((StreamEvent) -> Void)?) { self.onEvent = onEvent }
100	
101	  func consume(_ data: Data) {
102	    lock.lock()
103	    raw.append(data)
104	    var events: [StreamEvent] = []
105	    if onEvent != nil {
106	      pending.append(data)
107	      while let nl = pending.firstIndex(of: 0x0A) {
108	        let line = Data(pending[pending.startIndex..<nl])
109	        pending = Data(pending[(nl + 1)...])
110	        if let event = try? JSONDecoder().decode(StreamEvent.self, from: line) {
111	          events.append(event)
112	        }
113	      }
114	    }
115	    lock.unlock()
116	    if let onEvent { events.forEach(onEvent) }
117	  }
118	
119	  var rawString: String {
120	    lock.lock()
121	    defer { lock.unlock() }
122	    return String(data: raw, encoding: .utf8) ?? ""
123	  }
124	}

126	/// The subset of `WorkroomCLI` that `AppStore` drives, expressed as a protocol so
127	/// tests can inject a fake (issue #103). `WorkroomCLI` is the production conformer;
128	/// `bundledBinaryURL` and the process plumbing stay concrete (not used by AppStore).
129	protocol WorkroomCLIProtocol {
130	  func list(warnings: String, project: String?) async throws -> ListResponse
131	  func addProject(_ path: String, create: Bool) async throws -> String
132	  func create(
133	    project: String,
134	    onLog: ((String) -> Void)?,
135	    onReady: ((_ name: String, _ path: String, _ hasSetup: Bool) -> Void)?
136	  ) async throws -> CreateResponse
137	  func delete(name: String, project: String, onLog: ((String) -> Void)?) async throws
138	  func deleteProject(
139	    _ path: String, withWorkrooms: Bool, fromDisk: Bool, onLog: ((String) -> Void)?
140	  ) async throws -> [URL]
141	}
142	
143	/// Drives the bundled `workroom` binary over its `--json` contract. All work runs
144	/// off the main thread. Mutations are rare and one-shot; the binary itself forks to
145	/// git/jj, so the subprocess spawn is negligible.
146	final class WorkroomCLI: WorkroomCLIProtocol {
147	  static let shared = WorkroomCLI()
148	  private init() {}
149	
150	  // MARK: Public API
151	
152	  func list(warnings: String = "fast", project: String? = nil) async throws -> ListResponse {
153	    var args = ["list", "--json", "--warnings=\(warnings)"]
154	    if let project { args += ["--project", project] }
155	    let result = try await run(args, timeout: warnings == "full" ? 15 : 5)
156	    return try decode(ListResponse.self, from: result)
157	  }
158	
159	  /// Registers a project. With `create`, the CLI creates and git-initializes the
160	  /// directory if it does not already exist (issue #103); otherwise the path must
161	  /// already be a Git/JJ repo. Returns the canonical path the CLI registered (used
162	  /// to select the project after a reload). The git init + initial commit can take
163	  /// a moment, so the timeout is generous.
164	  func addProject(_ path: String, create: Bool) async throws -> String {
165	    var args = ["add-project", path, "--json"]
166	    if create { args.append("--create") }
167	    let result = try await run(args, timeout: 60)
168	    return try decode(AddProjectResponse.self, from: result).path
169	  }
170	
171	  /// Creates a workroom. `onReady(name, path, hasSetup)` fires when the workroom exists
172	  /// but setup is still running — `hasSetup` reports whether a setup script will run, so
173	  /// the caller can block on its log. `onLog` streams setup output lines as they arrive.
174	  @discardableResult
175	  func create(
176	    project: String,
177	    onLog: ((String) -> Void)? = nil,
178	    onReady: ((_ name: String, _ path: String, _ hasSetup: Bool) -> Void)? = nil
179	  ) async throws -> CreateResponse {
180	    // Setup scripts run inside this call, so resolve the user's environment first — freshly, in
181	    // case a tool was installed or a dotfile edited since launch. Usually already warm: the New
182	    // Workroom dialog kicks the same single-flighted probe when it opens.
183	    await ShellEnvironment.refresh()
184	    let result = try await run(
185	      ["create", "--json", "--no-editor", "--project", project], timeout: 600, userInitiated: true
186	    ) { event in
187	      switch event.type {
188	      case "log": if let text = event.text { onLog?(text) }
189	      case "created":
190	        if let name = event.name, let path = event.path {
191	          onReady?(name, path, event.setup ?? false)
192	        }
193	      default: break
194	      }
195	    }
196	    return try decode(CreateResponse.self, from: result)
197	  }
198	
199	  func delete(name: String, project: String, onLog: ((String) -> Void)? = nil) async throws {
200	    await ShellEnvironment.refresh()  // a teardown script may run inside this call
201	    let result = try await run(
202	      ["delete", name, "--json", "--project", project, "--confirm", name], timeout: 600,
203	      userInitiated: true
204	    ) { event in
205	      if event.type == "log", let text = event.text { onLog?(text) }
206	    }
207	    try throwIfError(result)
208	  }
209	
210	  /// Removes a project from the config. Three modes (mutually exclusive on disk):
211	  /// - default (config-only): nothing on disk is touched (worktree dirs, branches, files stay).
212	  /// - `withWorkrooms`: also tears down every registered workroom (hard-deletes worktree dirs +
213	  ///   files; branches are always kept), streaming teardown output via `onLog`.
214	  /// - `fromDisk`: runs each workroom's teardown, drops the project from config, and RETURNS the
215	  ///   directories (project root first, then workrooms) for the app to move to the Bin — the CLI
216	  ///   never deletes them itself (issue #108). The returned `[URL]` is empty in the other modes.
217	  ///
218	  /// `--confirm` echoes the path (the type-to-confirm guard lives in the sheet; this just
219	  /// satisfies the CLI gate).
220	  /// Whether a `delete-project` in this mode will run per-workroom teardown scripts. Only the
221	  /// cascading modes do; plain config-only removal touches nothing on disk, so it must not pay for
222	  /// a shell probe. Keyed on the same condition as the timeout below, and factored out so the
223	  /// gating decision is testable without spawning the bundled binary.
224	  static func deleteProjectRunsScripts(withWorkrooms: Bool, fromDisk: Bool) -> Bool {
225	    withWorkrooms || fromDisk
226	  }
227	
228	  @discardableResult
229	  func deleteProject(
230	    _ path: String, withWorkrooms: Bool, fromDisk: Bool, onLog: ((String) -> Void)? = nil
231	  ) async throws -> [URL] {
232	    var args = ["delete-project", path, "--json", "--confirm", path]
233	    if withWorkrooms { args.append("--with-workrooms") }
234	    if fromDisk { args.append("--from-disk") }
235	    let runsScripts = Self.deleteProjectRunsScripts(
236	      withWorkrooms: withWorkrooms, fromDisk: fromDisk)
237	    if runsScripts { await ShellEnvironment.refresh() }
238	    let result = try await run(
239	      args, timeout: runsScripts ? 600 : 15, userInitiated: runsScripts
240	    ) { event in
241	      if event.type == "log", let text = event.text { onLog?(text) }
242	    }
243	    guard fromDisk else {
244	      try throwIfError(result)
245	      return []
246	    }
247	    let response = try decode(DeleteProjectResponse.self, from: result)
248	    return (response.trashPaths ?? []).map { URL(fileURLWithPath: $0) }
249	  }
250	
251	  // MARK: Binary location
252	
253	  /// The bundled `workroom` binary in Contents/Resources (NOT Contents/MacOS — "workroom"
254	  /// would collide with the "Workroom" app executable on the case-insensitive filesystem),
255	  /// or a dev fallback next to the running executable. Static so `CommandLineInstaller` can
256	  /// resolve the same binary when symlinking it into the user's PATH.
257	  static func bundledBinaryURL() throws -> URL {
258	    if let url = Bundle.main.url(forResource: "workroom", withExtension: nil) {
259	      return url
260	    }
261	    let exeDir = Bundle.main.bundleURL.deletingLastPathComponent()
262	    let candidate = exeDir.appendingPathComponent("workroom")
263	    if FileManager.default.isExecutableFile(atPath: candidate.path) {
264	      return candidate
265	    }
266	    throw WorkroomCLIError.binaryMissing
267	  }
268	
269	  // MARK: Decoding
270	
271	  private func decode<T: Decodable>(_ type: T.Type, from result: CLIResult) throws -> T {
272	    try throwIfError(result)
273	    do {
274	      return try JSONDecoder().decode(type, from: result.stdout)
275	    } catch {
276	      throw WorkroomCLIError.decodeFailed(raw: String(data: result.stdout, encoding: .utf8) ?? "")
277	    }
278	  }
279	
280	  /// Inspects the result and throws if it represents a failure. The CLI writes one
281	  /// JSON envelope to stdout for both success and error; a non-zero exit means error.
282	  private func throwIfError(_ result: CLIResult) throws {
283	    // A child killed by a signal — our timeout's `terminate()` (SIGTERM), or a SIGTERM the
284	    // system delivers around sleep/wake — reports the *signal number* as `terminationStatus`,
285	    // not a CLI exit code. Surfacing that as "workroom exited with code 15" was wrong (15 ==
286	    // SIGTERM); treat it as a timeout so it isn't mistaken for a real CLI failure.
287	    if result.timedOut || result.signaled { throw WorkroomCLIError.timedOut }
288	    if result.exitCode == 0 { return }
289	    if let env = try? JSONDecoder().decode(Envelope.self, from: result.stdout),
290	      let body = env.error
291	    {
292	      throw WorkroomCLIError.cli(kind: body.kind, message: body.message)
293	    }
294	    throw WorkroomCLIError.nonzero(code: result.exitCode, stderr: result.stderr)
295	  }
296	
297	  // MARK: Process execution
298	
299	  /// Runs the helper with `args`, draining stdout (read to end for the single JSON
300	  /// envelope) and stderr (read incrementally so `onLog` fires per NDJSON line as the
301	  /// script runs) concurrently, and enforcing a timeout. On timeout the process is
302	  /// terminated then killed.
303	  ///
304	  /// `userInitiated` selects the environment the child gets. The commands that run the user's own
305	  /// setup/teardown scripts get the full probed environment, so those scripts see the shell they
306	  /// were written against. Everything else (`list`, `add-project`) takes PATH only — a cheap,
307	  /// frequent read has no reason to carry the user's whole environment.
308	  private func run(
309	    _ args: [String], timeout: TimeInterval, userInitiated: Bool = false,
310	    onEvent: ((StreamEvent) -> Void)? = nil
311	  ) async throws -> CLIResult {
312	    let url = try Self.bundledBinaryURL()
313	    return try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
314	      let proc = Process()
315	      proc.executableURL = url
316	      proc.arguments = args
317	
318	      var env: [String: String]
319	      if userInitiated {
320	        env = ShellEnvironment.environment()
321	      } else {
322	        env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
323	        env["PATH"] = ShellEnvironment.path()
324	      }
325	      env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
326	      env["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
327	      proc.environment = env
328	
329	      let outPipe = Pipe()
330	      let errPipe = Pipe()
331	      proc.standardOutput = outPipe
332	      proc.standardError = errPipe
333	
334	      let state = RunState()
335	      let collector = StderrCollector(onEvent: onEvent)
336	      let drain = DispatchGroup()
337	
338	      drain.enter()
339	      DispatchQueue.global().async {
340	        state.setStdout(outPipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile())
341	        drain.leave()
342	      }
343	
344	      drain.enter()
345	      errPipe.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = { handle in
346	        let data = handle.availableData
347	        if data.isEmpty {
348	          handle.readabilityHandler = nil  // EOF: pipe closed
349	          drain.leave()
350	          return
351	        }
352	        collector.consume(data)
353	      }
354	
355	      let timeoutItem = DispatchWorkItem {
356	        guard !state.isFinished, proc.isRunning else { return }
357	        state.markTimedOut()
358	        proc.terminate()
359	        // NOTE: full process-group kill (also reaping git/jj grandchildren)
360	        // would require launching via posix_spawn with setpgid; terminate() +
361	        // GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is sufficient for the MVP.
362	        DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 2) {
363	          if proc.isRunning { kill(proc.processIdentifier, SIGKILL) }
364	        }
365	      }
366	      DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout, execute: timeoutItem)
367	
368	      proc.terminationHandler = { finishedProc in
369	        state.markFinished()
370	        timeoutItem.cancel()
371	        drain.wait()
372	        continuation.resume(
373	          returning: CLIResult(
374	            stdout: state.stdout,
375	            stderr: collector.rawString,
376	            exitCode: finishedProc.terminationStatus,
377	            timedOut: state.timedOut,
378	            signaled: finishedProc.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal
379	          ))
380	      }
381	
382	      do {
383	        try proc.run()
384	      } catch {
385	        errPipe.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = nil
386	        continuation.resume(throwing: error)
387	      }
388	    }
389	  }
390	}

input.new_string:
### `SessionByteQueue`'s `wouldBlock` path has no dedicated test (macapp) — FIXED, 2026-08-16

Moved `SessionByteQueue` + `SessionIO` + the two outcome enums from `WorkroomSession/SessionSupport.swift`
into `WorkroomSessionProtocol/SessionIO.swift` (marked `public`) — the module already shared by
`WorkroomApp`, `WorkroomAppTests`, and `workroom-session`, per the second option this entry named.
`WorkroomAppTests/Session/SessionByteQueueTests.swift` now drives `drain`'s `wouldBlock` path against
a real, unread, non-blocking pipe (not a mock): a short write that would block, the queue left
correctly positioned, then a full flush once the reader catches up.

**Trap while writing the test:** the first version set only the pipe's WRITE end non-blocking. The
read-back loop's `SessionIO.read(readFD)` then blocked for real once the currently-buffered bytes
were drained — hanging the test host (`Workroom Dev.app`, beach-balling) rather than failing, since
the block happens deep inside a real `read()` syscall on the main test thread. Both ends of a pipe
used for this kind of poll-until-`wouldBlock` loop need `SessionIO.setNonBlocking`.

**Priority:** done.

  beta.23); the standalone CLI's own `darwin_amd64` tarball was always fine, only the embedded copy

`make app-run`/⌘R are unaffected by construction — `XCTestConfigurationFilePath` is set only by

## P3 — Tests and tooling

### `AppStore`'s default `cli` isn't hardened against a forgotten test double (macapp) — filed 2026-08-16

**What:** `AppStore.init(cli: WorkroomCLIProtocol? = nil, ...)` defaults an un-injected `cli` to the
real `WorkroomCLI.shared` — including under XCTest. A test that constructs a bare `AppStore()`,
leaves `projectStore.projects` empty, and calls `bootstrap()`/`reload()` would silently shell out to
the real bundled `workroom` binary and read the developer's actual `~/.config/workroom/config.json`.

**Why not fixed now:** traced every current call site (`AppStoreSessionRestoreTests`'s two
`bootstrap()` calls) — both pre-seed `projectStore.projects`, so `bootstrap` takes the
`apply(projectStore.projects)` branch and never reaches `cli.list`. Nothing is broken today; this is
defense against a future test, not a current bug. See the 2026-08-16 "Recently done" entry above for
the actual bug this session found and fixed (the shared window's own bootstrap, not this).

**How to start:** default the un-injected `cli` to a `WorkroomCLIProtocol` conformer, active only
under `XCTestConfigurationFilePath != nil`, whose every method throws immediately — a test that
forgot to inject a fake gets a loud, specific failure instead of a silent real-data read.

**Depends on:** nothing blocking.

**Priority:** P3 — hardening, not a known bug.

file.content:
APP_PROJECT := WorkroomApp.xcodeproj
APP_NAME    := Workroom Dev
APP_BUNDLE  := DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug/$(APP_NAME).app
APP_XCODEBUILD := xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomApp -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages

# Extra xcodebuild build-setting overrides, appended to app-build/app-test. Empty locally so
# ⌘R-style automatic signing is used; CI sets this to ad-hoc / no-team signing because hosted
# runners have no signing cert or DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (e.g.
# `make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="`).
APP_SIGN_FLAGS ?=

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-test. Parallel execution by default: the suite is dominated by a
# few slow integration classes (Markdown WebView renders, real git/jj repos), so spreading classes
# across worker processes cuts the run ~40% (48s -> ~29s). Each worker gets its own host-app process
# but they share one UserDefaults domain, so a test mutating a `Defaults` key another class reads
# would race — override with `make app-test APP_TEST_FLAGS=` to bisect a suspected parallel-only
# failure. Test dirs are already UUID-scoped under NSTemporaryDirectory, so those don't collide.
APP_TEST_FLAGS ?= -parallel-testing-enabled YES

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-uitest. Skips the 3 most expensive/flaky cases by default (each
# does a real quit+relaunch or a hard timing budget), since XCUITest never runs in CI and a routine
# `make app-uitest` was paying ~4-5 min for tests that are only load-bearing right before a release.
# The isolation-tripwire tests those two classes carried (proving discovery/session-restore no-op
# without a seeded path — a guard the REST of this suite depends on) were extracted to
# `AgentSessionIsolationTripwireUITests` first, so the routine sweep keeps that safety net. Run the
# full suite (pre-release, or after touching any of these) with `make app-uitest APP_UITEST_FLAGS=`.
APP_UITEST_FLAGS ?= -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips

# The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links, built into the local WrVcs SwiftPM package
# (vcs/swift/WrVcs). Must run before xcodegen so the package's xcframework + generated Swift exist.
# arm64 by default; release/distribution sets VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal (needs rustup stable >=
# 1.93 + both darwin targets, and `protoc` on PATH for jj-lib's build).
VCS_APPLE_FLAGS ?=
app-vcs: ## Build the Rust VCS core (xcframework + Swift bindings) the app links
	vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh $(VCS_APPLE_FLAGS)

app-run: app-build ## Build (Debug) and launch the dev app, replacing any running dev instance
	cd macapp || exit 1; \
	pkill -x "$(APP_NAME)" 2>/dev/null || true; \
	if pgrep -f "$(APP_NAME).app/Contents/MacOS/workroom-session" >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  echo "Stopping persisted $(APP_NAME) session daemon (its panes will come back empty)"; \
	  pkill -f "$(APP_NAME).app/Contents/MacOS/workroom-session" 2>/dev/null || true; \
	fi; \
	i=0; \
	while pgrep -x "$(APP_NAME)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ $$i -lt 40 ]; do \
	  sleep 0.2; i=$$((i + 1)); \
	done; \
	echo "Launching $(APP_BUNDLE)"; \
	open "$(APP_BUNDLE)"

app-build: app-vcs ## Build the app (Debug)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) build $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test: app-vcs ## Run the app's unit tests
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_TEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-uitest: app-vcs ## Run the app's UI tests (XCUITest — needs a real GUI login session, not headless)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_UITEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test-supervisor: ## Run the run-command supervisor PTY integration test (real shell + fake server)
	python3 macapp/Tests/run-supervisor/test_supervisor.py

app-test-scripts: ## Run the dependency-free shell-script tests (build-helper archs, channel classify)
	sh macapp/Scripts/build-helper_test.sh

301

304	IO-layer subsection. Everything else in §N — surface/split churn volume, workroom switch, workroom
305	delete, force-quit variant, the scrollbar overlay — is still manual-only, exactly as it was before
306	this bump. That gap isn't new; it's just now visible with a name, having been walked end-to-end this
307	session rather than assumed.
308	
309	**Two concrete blockers surfaced while running the manual retest, worth fixing before the next
310	attempt at automating this, not just re-discovering them again:**
311	- **Workroom-tab chips and the run-command button (`workroom.tab.*`, `runCommand.run`) didn't respond
312	  to synthetic `AXPress` or a raw `click at {x,y}` from an external AppleScript-driven session** —
313	  0 observable effect despite the action reporting success and the on-screen bounds being correct.
314	  Real keyboard shortcuts (⌘R/⇧⌘R) and raw `keystroke` text input worked fine throughout, which is
315	  how the QA results file's Run-tab and behavioral checks actually got driven. `GhosttyOrphanShellUITests`
316	  and `GhosttyActionDispatchUITests` prove an actual XCUITest host process (not external AppleScript)
317	  CAN drive these controls — `focusTerminal`'s tab-chip click works there. So the fix for
318	  workroom-switch/delete/OSC-7 automation is likely "write it as a real XCUITest," not "find the
319	  right AppleScript incantation."
320	- **`Process()` spawning `/bin/ps` (or presumably anything) throws `NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=1
321	  "Operation not permitted"` from inside an XCUITest runner** (`WorkroomAppUITests`'s auto-generated
322	  `XCTRunner` host is sandboxed against subprocess spawning; the app under test itself is not — two
323	  different sandbox realms). `GhosttyOrphanShellUITests` worked around this with a heartbeat FILE
324	  (`/tmp`, not `NSTemporaryDirectory()` — see that file's doc comment for why `NSTemporaryDirectory()`
325	  resolves to a different, container-private path in the runner vs. the app) instead of polling `ps`.
326	  Any future XCUITest needing to observe OS-level process state should reuse that pattern rather than
327	  rediscovering the `ps` restriction.
328

330	fine:** the terminfo `Se` capability's cursor-style-reset behavior change (`\E[2 q` → `\E[0 q`, found
331	during the bump's resource regen) has never been visually confirmed. A `screencapture -x` attempt at
332	this was abandoned mid-session when it turned out to capture the whole display rather than the
333	target window (see the bump entry above) — needs either a window-scoped capture API or a human at
334	the keyboard, not screen-wide automation.
335	
336	**Sharper target for whoever runs this, found while surveying the wider `332b2aef...35e1a016`
337	upstream range (not just the diff of the terminfo file itself):** the `Se` change isn't a one-time
338	fixed-escape swap. It was refined again after `\E[2 q`→`\E[0 q` — `Se` now restores whatever cursor
339	style/blink the engine is *configured* with, paired with new default-cursor-style/blink options
340	(ghostty `c19ce03b`, `42fcd58d`; both confirmed ancestors of our pinned `35e1a016`). So the right
341	check is "does resetting after a TUI exit return to Workroom's actual configured default," not
342	merely "does it emit `\E[0 q`" — a literal-escape assertion could pass while the dynamic-default
343	behavior is still unverified.
344	
345	**Depends on:** nothing blocking — can start anytime. The two platform-constraint findings above
346	mean whoever picks this up should design as a real XCUITest from the start, not attempt external
347	AppleScript driving again.

1508	layout decisions that **no test covers**: `.truncationMode(.head)` (keep the tail, because a
1509	repo-relative path's discriminating part is its filename and immediate directory) and

1516	  (documented at `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/HistoryCommitCardTests.swift:9-13`). `PaneRenderingTests`
1517	  works only because `GhosttySurfaceView` is a real `NSView` it can count.
1518	- **XCUITest** reads the accessibility *label*, which carries the full untruncated string no matter
1519	  what is actually drawn — so a test passes while the branch has collapsed to nothing on screen.

1522	on every theme and font change. So it's an eyeball check in the #136 verification steps: split a diff
1523	pane narrow and confirm the path keeps its filename while the branch truncates first.

### Pane-footer truncation is manual-verify only (macapp) — #136 follow-up

**What:** The pane footer's path segment (`TerminalStatusBar.pathSegment`) carries two deliberate
layout decisions that **no test covers**: `.truncationMode(.head)` (keep the tail, because a
repo-relative path's discriminating part is its filename and immediate directory) and
`.layoutPriority(1)` (the branch yields space before the path does).

**Why it's open:** neither test layer can see it.

- The **unit gate** can't assert SwiftUI text at all: macOS only materializes SwiftUI's a11y elements
  for a live AX client, so an `NSHostingView` in a test process reports an `AXGroup` with 0 children
  (documented at `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/HistoryCommitCardTests.swift:9-13`). `PaneRenderingTests`
  works only because `GhosttySurfaceView` is a real `NSView` it can count.
- **XCUITest** reads the accessibility *label*, which carries the full untruncated string no matter
  what is actually drawn — so a test passes while the branch has collapsed to nothing on screen.

Automating it would need image-snapshot testing, which this repo has none of and which would churn
on every theme and font change. So it's an eyeball check in the #136 verification steps: split a diff
pane narrow and confirm the path keeps its filename while the branch truncates first.

**Depends on:** nothing, but the entry above shrinks it — content panes are exempt from the 300pt
pane floor (`TerminalSessions.fits` returns `true` when there's no surface), which is what makes a
~198pt content pane reachable in the first place. Fix that and this gap mostly stops mattering.

**Priority:** P3 (degraded legibility in a narrow split; no data loss, no wrong information).

1900	syntax itself works (`Config.zig:9837` `Theme.parseCLI` — `light:`/`dark:` keys, both required,
1901	order-independent). But "the engine picks the variant itself" is false for a *live* surface:
1902	
1903	- Which variant applies is resolved once, at config-derive time, from `_conditional_state.theme`
1904	  (`Config.zig:4457`).
1905	- `ghostty_app_set_color_scheme`/`ghostty_surface_set_color_scheme` (App.zig `colorSchemeEvent`,
1906	  Surface.zig:4716 `colorSchemeCallback`) only **flip that state and fire a
1907	  `.reload_config{.soft=true}` action** — neither one re-derives the config itself.
1908	- `apprt/embedded.zig:267` `performAction` forwards every action straight to the host `action_cb`;
1909	  there is no internal embedded-apprt handler that re-derives on our behalf.
1910	- `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:127` doesn't handle `GHOSTTY_ACTION_RELOAD_CONFIG` — it falls into
1911	  `default:` → `logUnhandled` → returns `false`.
1912	
1913	So adopting this syntax needs either (a) implementing that action for both the app-scoped and
1914	surface-scoped case, which means calling `ghostty_app_update_config`/`ghostty_surface_update_config`
1915	back into the engine from inside `action_cb` while it's mid-`colorSchemeEvent` — the same kind of
1916	reentrancy-off-callback-stacks hazard flagged for surface teardown (see the libghostty-surface-free
1917	memory note) — or (b) keeping our own explicit `updateConfig` calls, where scheme-flip-before-derive
1918	becomes a newly load-bearing ordering invariant (today's `applyThemeToAll` calls `reloadConfig`
1919	*before* `setColorScheme`, which is harmless only because today's single-name theme has no

syntax itself works (`Config.zig:9837` `Theme.parseCLI` — `light:`/`dark:` keys, both required,
order-independent). But "the engine picks the variant itself" is false for a *live* surface:

- Which variant applies is resolved once, at config-derive time, from `_conditional_state.theme`
  (`Config.zig:4457`).
- `ghostty_app_set_color_scheme`/`ghostty_surface_set_color_scheme` (App.zig `colorSchemeEvent`,
  Surface.zig:4716 `colorSchemeCallback`) only **flip that state and fire a
  `.reload_config{.soft=true}` action** — neither one re-derives the config itself.
- `apprt/embedded.zig:267` `performAction` forwards every action straight to the host `action_cb`;
  there is no internal embedded-apprt handler that re-derives on our behalf.
- `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:127` doesn't handle `GHOSTTY_ACTION_RELOAD_CONFIG` — it falls into
  `default:` → `logUnhandled` → returns `false`.

So adopting this syntax needs either (a) implementing that action for both the app-scoped and
surface-scoped case, which means calling `ghostty_app_update_config`/`ghostty_surface_update_config`
back into the engine from inside `action_cb` while it's mid-`colorSchemeEvent` — the same kind of
reentrancy-off-callback-stacks hazard flagged for surface teardown (see the libghostty-surface-free
memory note) — or (b) keeping our own explicit `updateConfig` calls, where scheme-flip-before-derive
becomes a newly load-bearing ordering invariant (today's `applyThemeToAll` calls `reloadConfig`
*before* `setColorScheme`, which is harmless only because today's single-name theme has no
conditional state to get stale).

**Verdict:** not a fit for a pre-release stability batch. There's no bug behind the current
single-name-per-appearance path — it's shipped and correct — and the two ways to land the native
syntax are either an engine-callback reentrancy change or a same-risk reorder of existing calls, both
only verifiable by manually flip-testing OS appearance against live terminals. Re-pricing from "emit
both names once, drop `force:`" to "action-handling change with a re-entrancy hazard and a new
ordering invariant."

**Priority:** P2 → hold. Re-open only alongside deliberate engine-callback work, not as a drive-by.

3	// Pure geometry for the two horizontal tab strips — the terminal strip (`TerminalTabStrip`) and the
4	// Workrooms tab bar (`WorkroomTabBar`). Everything here is view-free so it's unit-testable, and
5	// shared so the two strips can't drift: drag-to-reorder (`TabReorder`, issue #23), the
6	// overflow/pinning decision and its constants (`TabStripOverflow` / `TabStripMetrics`, issue #129),
7	// and the split-group bracket's geometry (`TabStripSplitRun`).
8	
9	/// Pure drag-to-reorder math, shared by the terminal tab strip (`TerminalTabStrip`) and the
10	/// Workrooms tab bar (`WorkroomTabBar`, issue #23). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip` so the index
11	/// resolution and gap offsets are unit-testable without a view, and the two strips can't drift.
12	///
13	/// Operates on **position-indexed** chip widths (`widths[i]` is the natural width of the chip at
14	/// position `i`), so it's agnostic to what the chips are — terminal tabs (`UUID`) or workroom
15	/// targets (`String`). The caller maps its own model to a `[CGFloat]` before calling.
16	enum TabReorder {
17	  /// Where the dragged chip lands given its current translation: walk outward from `draggedIndex`,
18	  /// crossing each neighbour once the drag passes that neighbour's half-width (chip width +
19	  /// `spacing`). Reaches index 0 and the last slot.
20	  static func dropTargetIndex(
21	    widths: [CGFloat], draggedIndex di: Int, translation: CGFloat, spacing: CGFloat
22	  ) -> Int {
23	    var idx = di
24	    if translation > 0 {
25	      var accumulated: CGFloat = 0
26	      var j = di + 1
27	      while j < widths.count {
28	        let span = widths[j] + spacing
29	        if translation > accumulated + span / 2 {
30	          idx = j
31	          accumulated += span
32	          j += 1
33	        } else {
34	          break
35	        }
36	      }
37	    } else if translation < 0 {
38	      var accumulated: CGFloat = 0
39	      var j = di - 1
40	      while j >= 0 {
41	        let span = widths[j] + spacing
42	        if -translation > accumulated + span / 2 {
43	          idx = j
44	          accumulated += span
45	          j -= 1
46	        } else {
47	          break
48	        }
49	      }
50	    }
51	    return idx
52	  }
53	
54	  /// Horizontal shift for a non-dragged chip at `index` so the row opens a gap at the drop `target`.
55	  /// `amount` is the dragged chip's width plus inter-chip spacing.
56	  static func gapShift(index: Int, draggedIndex: Int?, target: Int?, amount: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
57	    guard let di = draggedIndex, let ti = target else { return 0 }
58	    if di < ti, index > di, index <= ti { return -amount }  // dragging right: slide left
59	    if di > ti, index >= ti, index < di { return amount }  // dragging left: slide right
60	    return 0
61	  }
62	}
63	
64	/// Shared drag-to-reorder STATE for a horizontal tab strip (issue #23), generic over the chip
65	/// identity type (`TerminalTab.ID` for `TerminalTabStrip`, `SidebarID` for `WorkroomTabBar`) — the
66	/// stateful choreography around `TabReorder`'s pure math, which had drifted into two
67	/// hand-synchronized copies. Both strips independently discovered and fixed the SAME bug: `commit`
68	/// must resolve off the gesture's own final translation, never the live `translation` this type
69	/// tracks for rendering, because a fast/coarse drag's last `onChanged` sample can land short of
70	/// `onEnded`'s true displacement. Each strip owns one `@State private var drag = TabReorderDrag<ID>()`
71	/// and supplies its own commit action and drop-into-pane wiring as call-site closures — the
72	/// division of labor `TabReorder` already uses successfully. Reorder-clamping (`WorkroomTabBar`'s
73	/// `clampReorder`, absent in `TerminalTabStrip`) stays a call-site transform on `finalTranslation`/
74	/// `translation`, not a flag on this type.
75	struct TabReorderDrag<ID: Hashable> {
76	  /// The chip currently dragging, or nil.
77	  private(set) var id: ID?
78	  /// Live translation for the render-time gap preview — NOT what `commit` resolves against.
79	  private(set) var translation: CGFloat = 0
80	  private(set) var widths: [ID: CGFloat] = [:]
81	
82	  var isDragging: Bool { id != nil }
83	
84	  /// The dragged chip's own measured width, or 0 while nothing is dragging / unmeasured.
85	  var draggedWidth: CGFloat { id.flatMap { widths[$0] } ?? 0 }
86	
87	  mutating func setWidths(_ widths: [ID: CGFloat]) { self.widths = widths }
88	
89	  /// `DragGesture.onChanged` handler: latches `id` on the first call for this drag (subsequent
90	  /// calls for a different id are ignored — mirrors both strips' `if draggingID == nil` guard),
91	  /// then records the live translation for the render pass.
92	  mutating func update(_ chipID: ID, translation: CGFloat) {
93	    if id == nil { id = chipID }
94	    guard id == chipID else { return }
95	    self.translation = translation
96	  }
97	
98	  /// Where the dragged chip would land right now, for the render-time gap preview. `nil` while
99	  /// nothing is dragging, the dragged id isn't present in `ids`, or `suspendedByPaneDrag` is true
100	  /// (a chip dragged down into a pane stops opening a reorder gap).
101	  func dropIndex(ids: [ID], spacing: CGFloat, suspendedByPaneDrag: Bool) -> Int? {
102	    guard !suspendedByPaneDrag, let id, let di = ids.firstIndex(of: id) else { return nil }
103	    return TabReorder.dropTargetIndex(
104	      widths: ids.map { widths[$0] ?? 0 }, draggedIndex: di, translation: translation,
105	      spacing: spacing)
106	  }
107	
108	  /// Resolve + clear the drag on drop. `finalTranslation` must be the gesture's own final value
109	  /// (`onEnded`'s `value.translation`), never `translation` above — see the type's doc. Returns
110	  /// the reorder to perform (`from`/`to` position indices), or `nil` when nothing was dragging or
111	  /// the drop index didn't move (a caller that always wants to call its move action anyway can
112	  /// ignore the nil case and use `id`/`ids.firstIndex(of:)` itself, but neither strip needs that).
113	  mutating func commit(ids: [ID], spacing: CGFloat, finalTranslation: CGFloat) -> (
114	    from: Int, to: Int
115	  )? {
116	    defer {
117	      id = nil
118	      translation = 0
119	    }
120	    guard let id, let di = ids.firstIndex(of: id) else { return nil }
121	    let ti = TabReorder.dropTargetIndex(
122	      widths: ids.map { widths[$0] ?? 0 }, draggedIndex: di, translation: finalTranslation,
123	      spacing: spacing)
124	    return ti != di ? (di, ti) : nil
125	  }
126	
127	  /// Clear the drag without resolving a reorder (e.g. dropped into a pane instead).
128	  mutating func cancel() {
129	    id = nil
130	    translation = 0
131	  }
132	}
133	
134	/// Geometry both tab strips must agree on (issue #129). One home, because the title-bar Workrooms bar
135	/// and the terminal strip are on screen at the same time — a fade or gutter that differs between them
136	/// is directly comparable, so a per-view copy of these numbers would drift visibly.
137	enum TabStripMetrics {
138	  /// Gap between the scrolling chip run and the pinned trailing controls, so a clipped chip never
139	  /// abuts them. Passed as the `spacing:` of the controls' `safeAreaInset`, which also *reserves* the
140	  /// controls' own width — so this is the only hand-set number in that relationship.
141	  static let gutter: CGFloat = 8
142	  /// Width of the dissolve at the scroller's trailing edge, so a clipped chip fades out instead of
143	  /// being cut mid-glyph. Deliberately equal to the scroll content's trailing inset: at full
144	  /// scroll-end the ramp then lands on empty margin and the last chip renders crisp, so the fade only
145	  /// ever dissolves content that really is cut off.
146	  static let fade: CGFloat = 8
147	  /// The *inline* "+"'s own leading pad (it hugs the last chip). Applied by the call site, not by the
148	  /// button, so the button's measured width stays free of positioning padding.
149	  static let inlineAddLead: CGFloat = 2
150	  /// Sub-pixel slack in the overflow comparison, so a live window resize can't thrash the mode on
151	  /// rounding alone.
152	  static let epsilon: CGFloat = 0.5
153	  /// Widest a chip's title renders before it tail-truncates (the ellipsis + tooltip carry the rest).
154	  /// One number for both strips *and* the workroom pane header, which deliberately matches them: all
155	  /// three can be on screen at once, so a per-view copy — this was three, each cross-referenced only by
156	  /// comment — is directly comparable and drifts visibly. Note a workroom chip spends it on two names
157	  /// (project + workroom) against a terminal chip's one, so it starts truncating sooner.
158	  static let maxChipTitle: CGFloat = 180
159	}
160	
161	/// The overflow decision for a horizontal tab strip (issue #129): does the *inline* layout — the chip
162	/// run with the "+" hugging the last chip — still fit the width available to it? When it doesn't, the
163	/// trailing controls lift out of the scroller and pin at its trailing edge, so the "+" is always
164	/// reachable.
165	enum TabStripOverflow {
166	  /// Natural width of a chip run: every chip plus the inter-chip spacing.
167	  static func runWidth(_ widths: [CGFloat], spacing: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
168	    guard !widths.isEmpty else { return 0 }
169	    return widths.reduce(0, +) + spacing * CGFloat(widths.count - 1)
170	  }
171	
172	  /// Whether the trailing controls must pin.
173	  ///
174	  /// Takes **only** quantities that are independent of where those controls currently sit, so the
175	  /// answer cannot depend on the layout it selects: the predicate has one fixed point and cannot
176	  /// oscillate as the window resizes. There is deliberately no `isPinned` parameter — a
177	  /// "scroll content vs viewport" comparison *would* oscillate, because lifting the controls out
178	  /// shrinks the content and the viewport by different amounts, leaving a band of widths that pins,
179	  /// then fits, then pins.
180	  ///
181	  /// - Parameters:
182	  ///   - runWidth: measured width of the whole chip run **including the trailing divider and its
183	  ///     pads** — the divider lives inside the measured run and is toggled by opacity, never removed,
184	  ///     so it is always laid out. Passing a chips-only width would let the boundary tests pass while
185	  ///     the rendered threshold sits a few points off.
186	  ///   - add: the trailing controls' intrinsic width, without any positioning pad.
187	  ///   - available: width the strip has for the chips + controls (its own width minus any
188	  ///     fixed-size sibling such as the per-tab toolbar).
189	  ///   - leadingInset: the row's leading inset (4pt in a workroom split, else 8pt).
190	  ///   - inlineAddLead: gap between the run and the controls while inline (spacing + their own pad).
191	  static func pinsControls(
192	    runWidth: CGFloat, add: CGFloat, available: CGFloat,
193	    leadingInset: CGFloat, inlineAddLead: CGFloat, gutter: CGFloat = TabStripMetrics.gutter,
194	    epsilon: CGFloat = TabStripMetrics.epsilon
195	  ) -> Bool {
196	    // Nothing measured yet (first layout pass): render inline. Every input is branch-independent, so
197	    // the correction that follows happens exactly once — it can't become a loop.
198	    guard available > 0, runWidth > 0, add > 0 else { return false }
199	    let inlineWidth = leadingInset + runWidth + inlineAddLead + add + gutter
200	    return inlineWidth > available + epsilon
201	  }
202	}
203	
204	/// Geometry of a split group's contiguous chip run within a strip — the `x`/`width` of the rounded
205	/// bracket drawn around the members (issue #3). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip.splitRunRect` so the
206	/// arithmetic is unit-testable without a view, and so it shares one summation with
207	/// `TabStripOverflow.runWidth` instead of carrying a second copy of it.
208	enum TabStripSplitRun {
209	  /// - Parameters:
210	  ///   - widths: position-indexed chip widths (`widths[i]` is the chip at position `i`).
211	  ///   - memberIndices: positions of the group's members. Guaranteed contiguous by the caller's
212	  ///     display order; only the first and last are used, so a stray gap is spanned rather than
213	  ///     rejected.
214	  ///   - spacing: the strip's inter-chip spacing.
215	  /// - Returns: `nil` when there's no real split (fewer than two members) or the indices are out of
216	  ///   range — both mean "draw no bracket".
217	  static func rect(widths: [CGFloat], memberIndices: [Int], spacing: CGFloat)
218	    -> (x: CGFloat, width: CGFloat)?
219	  {
220	    guard memberIndices.count >= 2,
221	      let first = memberIndices.min(), let last = memberIndices.max(),
222	      first >= 0, last < widths.count
223	    else { return nil }
224	    // x: everything before the first member, chips + the spacing that follows each of them.
225	    var x: CGFloat = 0
226	    for i in 0..<first { x += widths[i] + spacing }
227	    // width: the members' own chips, plus the spacing *between* them (one fewer gap than chips).
228	    var width: CGFloat = 0
229	    for i in first...last { width += widths[i] }
230	    width += spacing * CGFloat(last - first)
231	    return (x, width)
232	  }
233	}

### `WindowDragUITests.testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips` is a known gesture-timing flake — IMPROVED, still flaky, still skipped

**What:** Reproduced a pass then a fail on two consecutive back-to-back reruns of the identical test
against the identical binary during the beta.24 release gate — nothing else running, same machine,
same window geometry. Not caused by the beta.24 geometry fixes (fixture window 1200→1450pt): the
test computes its drag distance from the chips' own on-screen positions, so it's width-independent.

**Real bug found and fixed along the way:** `WorkroomTabBar.commitDrag`/`TerminalTabStrip.commitDrag`
computed the reorder's drop index from the `dragTranslation` **state**, which is only ever written
inside `onChanged` — so a drag whose LAST `onChanged` sample landed short of the true release point
(any coarse/fast delivery, synthetic or real) commits off a stale, under-shot translation instead of
the gesture's own accurate final `value.translation` at `onEnded`. Fixed in both strips (they
deliberately mirror each other's reorder math) to read `value.translation` directly at commit time.
Correct regardless of whether it's THE cause of this flake — verified via the full `WindowDragUITests`
+ `WorkroomStatus*`/`VCSProviderConformanceTests` suites, no regressions.

**Measured, three iterations, ~30 back-to-back reruns total:**
1. The `commitDrag` fix alone: 1/5 passed. Ruled out as a full fix on its own.
2. + polling `chipsByX` until two reads agree (ruling out a race against the strip's own 0.2s
   reorder-settle `withAnimation`): 3/5.
3. + switching the gesture from the touch-oriented `press(forDuration:thenDragTo:…)` to the
   macOS-native mouse `click(forDuration:thenDragTo:…)` (same API family, `XCUICoordinateMouseEvents`,
   available on macOS): **9/10 in clean, uncontaminated batches** (one batch's first two runs were
   invalidated by an unrelated concurrent edit to `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift` mid-build — excluded).

**Still flaky — deliberately left skipped.** ~90% is a real improvement over the original coin-flip,
but not deterministic, and a ~1-in-10 spurious red X right before a release is its own cost. The
`APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip entry (`Makefile:67`) stays as-is.

**How to fix further (not attempted):** the TODO's original two ideas — a manual multi-step drag
giving the reorder logic more interpolated samples, or loosening the swap threshold's dependency on
event count — remain open, on top of whatever residual gap the native-mouse switch didn't close.
Low priority: single test, single known flake mode, not client-facing.

under-shot final sample) is real-mouse-only — no synthetic test can prove a fast real flick commits
the true endpoint. Run a manual fast-flick drag test in both `TerminalTabStrip` and `WorkroomTabBar`
before trusting this beyond the automated numbers above.

**Second real bug found doing that manual check, 2026-08-16 — FIXED.** The reorder itself always
landed correctly; what the manual flick surfaced was a visual glitch on the SUCCESS path: the dragged
chip visibly flicked back to its pre-drag position for one frame, THEN the reorder animated it to its
new home — reads as "the drag failed, then something else moved it." Root cause: both strips'
commit function called `drag.commit(...)` (which resets `drag.id`/`translation` — the state driving
the dragged chip's `offsetX` — as a side effect) OUTSIDE the `withAnimation` block, and wrapped only
the resulting `moveTab`/order-write inside it. The offset-reset therefore applied instantly,
unanimated, one render pass before the reorder's own animated transition started. Fixed by moving the
`drag.commit(...)` call itself inside `withAnimation` in both `TerminalTabStrip.swift` and
`WorkroomTabBar.commitDrag`, so the offset resetting to 0 and the array reordering land in the same
animated transaction — one continuous motion from under the cursor to the new slot, whether or not a
reorder actually resulted.

**Re-measuring the flake rate while verifying this, same day:** got 7/12 fails with the fix, then (to
rule out a regression) 4/8 fails on the ORIGINAL unfixed code — both far worse than the "9/10" figure
above. `uptime` showed a load average of 7+ at the time (this machine had been running back-to-back
`xcodebuild` invocations for hours). Confirms the fix isn't the cause and the flake is genuinely
load-sensitive, not a fixed ~10% — the original measurement's "clean, uncontaminated batches" caveat
undersold how much machine load moves this number. Re-verify on a quiet machine before trusting any
future pass-rate measurement of this test.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/.claude/skills/curate-release

Tag-driven (see README "Releases"). After a release publishes, **curate its GitHub release
notes** — replace GoReleaser's raw commit list with a succinct, themed summary in the style of
`v2.0.0-beta.1` (a headline, a one-line framing, and grouped bullets). The commit list is what
the git log is for.

**Never hard-wrap paragraph or bullet text at a fixed column.** Write each paragraph and each
bullet as one unbroken line, however long. The in-app "What's New" viewer renders a literal `\n`
as a line break instead of reflowing it, so a source line wrapped at ~90 cols shows up as a
sentence broken mid-clause. Markdown block structure (headers, blank lines between paragraphs,
`-` bullets, blockquotes) is unaffected — only the wrapping *within* a block must go.

**Release channels** (issue #91) ship as **two products**. The **main** product (`workroom` CLI +
"Workroom" app) tracks `stable` or `pre`, chosen at runtime (`workroom update --channel stable|pre`;
the app's Settings picker). **Nightly** is a **separate side-by-side install** — a `workroom-nightly`
binary (baked `-X main.channel=nightly`) and a distinct "Workroom Nightly" app (`Nightly` build
config in `project.yml`: bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, `AppIcon-Nightly`, `WorkroomReleaseChannel`
Info.plist marker). Channel is a runtime pref for stable/pre, a build identity for nightly, so
nothing can drift/collide (the main binary rejects `--channel nightly`).

Canonical tag→channel classification is `internal/channel` (Go), mirrored by
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ReleaseChannel.swift` and `macapp/Scripts/channel-helper.sh` — **keep the
three in lockstep**. The updater selects per channel (stable = `/releases/latest` for byte-parity;
pre = `/releases` list, newest stable-or-prerelease; nightly = the fixed `nightly` release by tag),
orders nightlies by the monotonic commit-count and everything else by semver, and verifies against
`checksums.txt`. Nightly is a scheduled build (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, daily cron;
`CONFIGURATION=Nightly make app-release`) on a fixed `nightly` prerelease; all appcast-writing
workflows share a `concurrency: appcast-feed` group.

content.content:
## Signing & distribution

The project is configured for team **B898J443L9**:
- **Debug** (`⌘R`): automatic signing with your *Apple Development* cert.
- **Release**: manual signing with *Developer ID Application*, hardened runtime, secure
  timestamp. `Scripts/build-helper.sh` signs the embedded helper the same way before the
  app's final signature.

To produce a notarized, stapled `Workroom.dmg` installer (the app inside is notarized +
stapled too), first install `create-dmg` and store notary credentials once (app-specific
password from appleid.apple.com — not your Apple ID password):

```bash
brew install create-dmg
xcrun notarytool store-credentials "workroom-notary" \
    --apple-id "you@example.com" --team-id B898J443L9 --password "abcd-efgh-ijkl-mnop"
```

Then:

```bash
make app-release   # Release build → notarize → staple → drag-to-Applications DMG (Scripts/release.sh)
```

CI authenticates notarytool with an App Store Connect API key instead of the keychain
profile — set `NOTARY_KEY_PATH` (a `.p8`), `NOTARY_KEY_ID`, and `NOTARY_ISSUER_ID` and the
script uses those automatically.

Prefer not to use XcodeGen? Create a SwiftUI macOS App target manually, add the
libghostty-spm package, add the `WorkroomApp/` sources, and add `Scripts/build-helper.sh`
as a Run Script phase **after Compile Sources**.

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

The app self-updates via [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org): it polls an *appcast* feed and
installs newer, EdDSA-signed DMGs. Wiring lives in `Core/Updater.swift` (the "Check for
Updates…" menu item and the Settings toggle); the `SU*` keys in `project.yml` set the feed URL,
the public key, and automatic checks (on by default). The update artifact is the same notarized
DMG we ship, signed with an Ed25519 key whose **public** half is embedded as `SUPublicEDKey`.

The appcast is hosted as `appcast.xml` on a fixed **`appcast`** GitHub release
(`…/releases/download/appcast/appcast.xml`); each `v*` release appends an item to it via
`Scripts/appcast.sh`. Versioning is tag-driven: `release.sh` sets `CFBundleShortVersionString`
from the tag and `CFBundleVersion` to the commit count (monotonic, so Sparkle always sees a newer
release as an upgrade).

The update dialog renders each item's `<description>`, which holds the GitHub release notes.
Because those notes are curated *after* the release publishes (the release ships with goreleaser's
raw commit list), the `appcast-notes` workflow re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from
the release's current body on every `release: edited` event — so editing a release's notes
refreshes the in-app changelog automatically. Fix a published feed by hand with
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

name: Release

  macapp:

{"tag_name":"v2.0.0-beta.1","target_commitish":"master","name":"v2.0.0-beta.1","body":"## workroom 2.0 — now with a native macOS app

The headline of 2.0 is a **native macOS app** (macOS 14+): a SwiftUI interface with a
project → workroom sidebar and embedded terminals. The CLI ships bundled, so app users
don't need a separate install — and it stays fully standalone for terminal-first use on
macOS, Linux, and Windows.

> ⚠️ This is a beta — expect rough edges.

### macOS app
- Project → workroom tree sidebar, with an always-available project root
- Embedded terminals: multiple tabs per workroom, drag-to-reorder, copy-on-select,
  ⌘-click to open file paths, and activity notifications
- "Open in…" menu that remembers your last editor; offer to open new workrooms in `$EDITOR`
- Streamed setup/teardown script output in a log panel
- Settings window, light/dark/system theme, and Sparkle auto-updates
- "Install workroom Command in PATH" helper, plus a new app icon

### CLI
- New setup/teardown script env vars: `WORKROOM_PATH` and `WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH`
- Machine-readable `--json` API that powers the app

### Build & CI
- GitHub Actions CI; runs macOS app tests/lint and ships a notarized DMG
- `golangci-lint` and `swift-format` wired in

{"tag_name":"v2.0.0-beta.1","target_commitish":"master","name":"v2.0.0-beta.1","body":"## workroom 2.0 — now with a native macOS app

The headline of 2.0 is a **native macOS app** (macOS 14+): a SwiftUI interface with a
project → workroom sidebar and embedded terminals. The CLI ships bundled, so app users
don't need a separate install — and it stays fully standalone for terminal-first use on
macOS, Linux, and Windows.

> ⚠️ This is a beta — expect rough edges.

### macOS app
- Project → workroom tree sidebar, with an always-available project root
- Embedded terminals: multiple tabs per workroom, drag-to-reorder, copy-on-select,
  ⌘-click to open file paths, and activity notifications
- "Open in…" menu that remembers your last editor; offer to open new workrooms in `$EDITOR`
- Streamed setup/teardown script output in a log panel
- Settings window, light/dark/system theme, and Sparkle auto-updates
- "Install workroom Command in PATH" helper, plus a new app icon

### CLI
- New setup/teardown script env vars: `WORKROOM_PATH` and `WORKROOM_ROOT_PATH`
- Machine-readable `--json` API that powers the app

### Build & CI
- GitHub Actions CI; runs macOS app tests/lint and ships a notarized DMG
- `golangci-lint` and `swift-format` wired in
- Unified, namespaced root `Makefile`

input.content:
## Persistent terminal sessions

The headline of this beta: ordinary terminals now survive quitting the app. A new background session daemon keeps your shells running independently of the app process, so reattaching after a relaunch picks up exactly where you left off — scrollback and all — replacing the old scrollback-sidecar approach entirely.

> ⚠️ This is a beta — expect rough edges.

### macOS app
- Ordinary terminals persist across quit and relaunch; reattach forces a genuine redraw so a TUI never comes back blank, and titles/cwd/agent-footer usage survive the restart too
- Agent usage: quota and pace now show live in the terminal footer, with a detail popover on tap ("Background sessions" renamed to "Persist sessions" in Settings, with an explanation of what it does)
- libghostty engine bumped 1.2.3 → 1.3.2 (332b2aef → 35e1a016) — fixes a real memory leak in accessibility reads, confirmed with before/after leak counts
- Menu bar icon now matches the square-blocks logo
- Status-aware avatar image loader replaces `AsyncImage`, fixing a stale in-flight-fetch overwrite and an LRU eviction bug
- Tab reorder drag: fixed committing off a stale mid-drag position instead of the gesture's true release point, and a visible flick-back before the reorder animated in
- Working-copy diffs now combine staged and unstaged edits into one view instead of only showing one side
- A stopped run pane now warns instead of silently closing when its command is cleared; a dead supervisor respawn correctly reports stopped instead of looking still-running
- The files panel and diff viewer no longer rebuild/recompute on every unrelated store update

### CLI
- `list`/`list --json` warning logic unified, fixing a real divergence between the two
- `update` now sets the right command context for its JSON error envelope

{"tag_name":"v2.0.0-beta.25","target_commitish":"master","name":"v2.0.0-beta.25","body":"## Persistent terminal sessions

The headline of this beta: ordinary terminals now survive quitting the app. A new background session daemon keeps your shells running independently of the app process, so reattaching after a relaunch picks up exactly where you left off — scrollback and all — replacing the old scrollback-sidecar approach entirely.

> ⚠️ This is a beta — expect rough edges.

### macOS app
- Ordinary terminals persist across quit and relaunch; reattach forces a genuine redraw so a TUI never comes back blank, and titles/cwd/agent-footer usage survive the restart too
- Agent usage: quota and pace now show live in the terminal footer, with a detail popover on tap ("Background sessions" renamed to "Persist sessions" in Settings, with an explanation of what it does)
- libghostty engine bumped 1.2.3 → 1.3.2 (332b2aef → 35e1a016) — fixes a real memory leak in accessibility reads, confirmed with before/after leak counts
- Menu bar icon now matches the square-blocks logo
- Status-aware avatar image loader replaces `AsyncImage`, fixing a stale in-flight-fetch overwrite and an LRU eviction bug
- Tab reorder drag: fixed committing off a stale mid-drag position instead of the gesture's true release point, and a visible flick-back before the reorder animated in
- Working-copy diffs now combine staged and unstaged edits into one view instead of only showing one side
- A stopped run pane now warns instead of silently closing when its command is cleared; a dead supervisor respawn correctly reports stopped instead of looking still-running
- The files panel and diff viewer no longer rebuild/recompute on every unrelated store update

### CLI
- `list`/`list --json` warning logic unified, fixing a real divergence between the two
- `update` now sets the right command context for its JSON error envelope

Release notes curated, replacing the raw commit list — headline is persistent terminal sessions (the background session daemon work), plus tab-drag fix, libghostty bump, agent-usage footer, avatar loader, and the CLI warning-logic fix.

https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom/releases/tag/v2.0.0-beta.25
